final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful and more accurate than an unqualified compliance claim: it concedes that aggregate readiness evidence supports launch viability in general, while the materiality basis for omitting disclosure remains disputed and unresolved. But that narrower framing is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats here, because the missing item is not merely a disclosure-quality caveat or documentation nuance; it is an unresolved compliance predicate in the release policy itself. The admissible evidence shows a material limitation affecting a named launch use case tied to two servicer pilot commitments, with open legal review and no evidence of resolution, approved risk acceptance, or actual disclosure. On this record, certification without material-weakness disclosure remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence resolves the policy predicate requiring disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case.
The mortgage servicing assistant segment still misses target by 1.1 percentage points and is tied to two servicer pilot commitments, which supports materiality under the stated policy text.
Legal review remains open, so the record still lacks a final determination on whether disclosure is required.

Aggregate readiness passing by 2.3 percentage points and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch viability, but they do not satisfy the specific disclosure-policy condition.
The product note describing the segment as 5% of projected first-month traffic does not defeat materiality where customer commitments and pending legal review exist.
